answer:
Let \(D_i\) be the number of decodings of the prefix of length \(i\). Set

\[
D_0=1
\]

since the empty prefix has one decoding. For \(i\ge 1\),

\[
D_i =
\begin{cases}
D_{i-1} & \text{if } s_i\ne 0,\\
0 & \text{if } s_i=0,
\end{cases}
+
\begin{cases}
D_{i-2} & \text{if } i\ge2 \text{ and } 10s_{i-1}+s_i\in[10,26],\\
0 & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

The first term takes one digit; the second takes two digits as a code. The two-digit case automatically forbids a leading zero because the value must be at least \(10\).

Constant-space iteration:

```text
twoBack = 0     // D[i-2]
oneBack = 1     // D[i-1], initially D[0] = 1

for each digit at position i from 1 to n:
    cur = 0
    if digit != 0:
        cur += oneBack
    if i >= 2:
        v = 10 * previousDigit + digit
        if 10 <= v <= 26:
            cur += twoBack
    twoBack = oneBack
    oneBack = cur

return oneBack
```

### Trace for `10120`

| \(i\) | digit | single-digit term | two-digit term | \(D_i\) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | — | — | — | 1 |
| 1 | 1 | \(D_0=1\) | — | 1 |
| 2 | 0 | 0 | `10` valid: \(D_0=1\) | 1 |
| 3 | 1 | \(D_2=1\) | `01` invalid | 1 |
| 4 | 2 | \(D_3=1\) | `12` valid: \(D_2=1\) | 2 |
| 5 | 0 | 0 | `20` valid: \(D_3=1\) | 1 |

So `10120` has **1** decoding:

\[
10\mid1\mid20 = JAT
\]

### Trace for `100`

| \(i\) | digit | single-digit term | two-digit term | \(D_i\) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | — | — | — | 1 |
| 1 | 1 | \(D_0=1\) | — | 1 |
| 2 | 0 | 0 | `10` valid: \(D_0=1\) | 1 |
| 3 | 0 | 0 | `00` invalid | 0 |

So `100` has **0** decodings.
